grading_mode is the only mode setting

There is no per-target feedback setting. Every
registered target wants AI feedback by default,
and the instructor's test suite opts individual
targets out at run time by calling
ai_not_needed. A target she never wants
feedback on simply is not registered here.
The identifiers registered here are a
contract with her test suite.** She passes
these exact strings to ai_not_needed and
add_test_result. Rename one and her suite
stops matching, so the API rejects unknown
For the instructor guide: IMMEDIATE puts LLM
timeout, and submissions spike before a
deadline. Large courses should prefer NIGHTLY.
[for each method or class to grade]
She does not designate source files. The AI
phase derives the file from the target's
identifier, its kind and the assignment's
language (AD-12), so a pattern here would
A FILE-kind target's identifier IS the glob,
which covers the case where one target spans
Resolution must land on exactly one file.
Zero or several is a feedback failure the
student sees, so an identifier that does not
match the assignment's layout shows up
quickly rather than producing vague feedback
Attach rubric and feedback guidance [FR-4, FR-5, FR-13]
feedback rows reference rubric_id, so feedback
generated last week stays explainable after an
functional pass/fail, so FR-8, FR-9 and FR-10
are servable without deriving anything from AI
Three more columns tell the blank-looking
feedback cases apart: ai_needed false means her
suite opted the target out; completed_at NULL
means the nightly rerun has not happened yet;
last_error set means the attempt ran and
failed, and the student has already been told
Coverage depends on her calling add_test_result.
It is optional, so a suite that never calls it
leaves this view empty. Say so in the
instructor guide rather than letting an empty
generated feedback before the student sees it?
Mode-dependent. In NIGHTLY there is now a
natural place to put an approval gate: the
instructor approving a submission IS setting
ai_authorized_at, which AD-11 already uses as
the signal to grade. So "hold until approved"
needs no new mechanism, just a different actor
In IMMEDIATE there is no window at all:
feedback reaches the student in the same run
